title: You Worship Something You Just Dont Know It
author: The Best Leadership Newsletter
source: The Best Leadership Newsletter Ever (bytitleonly.substack.com), August 24, 2026
summary: Opening with the Aztec practice of human sacrifice, this piece builds on David Foster Wallace's commencement-speech line that "there is no such thing as not worshipping" to argue every leader has an unconscious "god" — something they'd sacrifice other things to protect — whether or not they can name it. Drawing on years of coaching leaders, the author identifies three common leadership gods: being needed (which blocks delegation and rest), being right (tied to imposter syndrome and the need to be the smartest person in the room), and the number (revenue, followers, views — a goal that never feels satisfied). The diagnostic he proposes isn't what someone has gained but what they've been willing to sacrifice for it. He turns the lens on himself, confessing that his own assumed god (money) turned out to be a false lead, and that his real god was acceptance — a need to be liked that cost him years of suppressed, inauthentic opinions. The piece doesn't argue for eliminating worship, which Wallace considered impossible, but for consciously naming and choosing what's on the altar instead of feeding it by default.
points: Building on David Foster Wallace's "everybody worships something," the author argues every leader has an unconscious "god" — the thing they'd sacrifice other things to protect — whether or not they recognize it.

Three common leadership "gods" are named: being needed (which blocks delegation), being right (tied to imposter syndrome), and the number (revenue, followers, views — a goal that never feels satisfied).

The diagnostic isn't what someone gains but what they're willing to sacrifice for it; the author's own confession is that his god was acceptance, which cost him years of suppressed authentic opinions.
The piece doesn't argue for eliminating worship (impossible, per Wallace) but for consciously choosing what's on the altar instead of defaulting into it unexamined.
quotes: There is no such thing as not worshipping. Everybody worships. The only choice we get is what to worship.
There are the people who worship being needed. They're the ones who can't delegate well. Heck, they can't even take a real vacation.
A god isn’t defined by what you love. It’s defined by what you’re willing to sacrifice for it.
So if you want to know what someone actually worships, don't ask them what they've gained. Ask what they've sacrificed.
The leader who worships being needed sacrifices growth - both theirs and their teams. The one who worships the number sacrifices connection with the people around them.

I needed to be liked. I needed to fit in with every person I met. I'd become whoever the room demanded I be. I'd shift my opinions, laugh at things I didn't think were funny, agree with things I knew were wrong.
You can acknowledge what you've been sacrificing. The relationships. The time. The health. The honesty. The people who trusted you and got sacrificed instead.
